subject: Discovery recap: Inference cost pressure & next steps (FinBot)
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Turner <alex.turner@finbot.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 20 Apr 2026 15:10:00 -0700
Subject: Discovery recap: Inference cost pressure & next steps (FinBot)

Alex — thanks again for the intro call this morning. Short recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment.

Summary of pain points you shared:
- Unit economics are the primary blocker: current per-inference cost is driving downgrade of model fidelity across prod flows.
- Peak/steady traffic patterns are spiky (morning/eod), and your current infra is struggling to keep latency p95 below 200ms when batching happens.
- Ops overhead: maintaining in-house Triton endpoints + custom autoscaling is consuming SRE cycles.

Current stack (as I heard it):
- Self-hosted Triton on A100s (on-prem colo) + a small burstable cloud pool for peak hours.
- Model: mix of a 13B instruction-tuned open model for customer-facing chat; experimenting with 70B for high-value flows but costs are prohibitive.
- Some 4-bit quantization in experiments, but not widely deployed due to accuracy concerns.

Success criteria you mentioned:
- Reduce per-inference unit cost by ~2.5-3x while keeping end-to-end user-perceived accuracy within ~2% of baseline.
- Maintain p95 latency under 200ms for main chat path (50-90 tokens typical).
- Clear audit trail / SOC2 evidence for procurement.

What Redwood can do (high-level):
- Routing & fallback to lower-cost model variants for non-critical flows.
- Prefix/KV caching and workload-aware batching to reduce token compute.
- Quantization + tuned kernels and kernel selection to reduce GPU memory and throughput costs.

Agreed next steps:
1) Tech deep-dive: Rishi (infra) + Ben (solutions) join a 60-min session to walk traces and run initial perf/cost estimations. Proposed slot: Thu 2026-04-22 10:00 PT — does that work?
2) You to share sample workload traces (token distribution, QPS, peak windows) and any recent perf reports.
3) We’ll produce a 1-page initial cost model + scoped pilot plan and share SOC2 summary for procurement.

Attachments: SOC2_summary_2025.pdf (SOC2 evidence we discussed) — will send in follow-up.

Thanks — quick replies welcome if the summary is off.

—
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0123
From: Alex Turner <alex.turner@finbot.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Samir Gupta <samir.gupta@finbot.ai>
Date: Wed, 21 Apr 2026 09:24:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Discovery recap: Inference cost pressure & next steps (FinBot)

Marissa — thanks for the thorough recap, looks great and aligned. A few clarifications / additions on our side: 

Current metrics: 
- Avg daily requests: ~120k (chat messages), avg tokens/request ~65, tail spikes up to ~400k on promo days.
- Latency target: p95 <200ms for chat; p50 goal is <80ms.
- Error budget: very low for fraud-detection flows (we’ll separate those).

Stack details: 
- Primary model: custom-tuned 13B (instruction tuned) for general chat; experimental 70B for high-value support flows.
- Serving: Triton on-prem (4x A100s), autoscaling via homegrown scheduler; cloud burst to GCP with managed instances.
- Caching: minimal prefix caching today. Token-level batching in some non-prod paths.

Quantization openness: we are open to 4-bit quantization if you can demonstrate <2% accuracy delta on our eval set. Also open to mixed-precision for the 70B experimental path if latency/cost tradeoffs are clear.

I’ll upload a 24-hour sample trace and our baseline perf spreadsheet to the shared Drive link by EOD. Thu 10am PT works for us.

Attachment: finbot_sample_trace_20260421.json (sample trace)

Looking forward — Alex
Alex Turner
VP Product, FinBot
alex.turner@finbot.ai | +1 (650) 555-9876

Perfect — thanks Alex. I got the sample trace and uploaded it to the Drive link you gave.

Prep requests for the deep-dive (so we can make the session productive):
- 24-hour trace + token histograms (you mentioned you’ll upload these)
- Baseline perf spreadsheet (p50/p95 by endpoint)

I’ll also attach an initial estimate and SOC2 summary for procurement (see attachments).

See you Thursday — Marissa
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 22 Apr 2026 08:15:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Discovery recap: Inference cost pressure & next steps (FinBot)

Rishi / Ben — forwarding the thread and Alex’s sample trace (link in thread). Key asks for the deep-dive:

- Please prepare a first-pass cost model that shows per-inference cost for: current setup (estimated), Redwood baseline with batching & caching, and Redwood with 4-bit quantization (expected). Present numbers as $/1000 inferences and a monthly projection at current avg traffic.
- Validate feasibility of p95 <200ms under our proposed batching configs (we may need a mixed configuration: small batch/low-latency pool + larger batch for non-critical flows).
- Quick checklist of SOC2 evidence items we should surface to procurement.

I’ll run the session and handle product/contract questions. Ben — can you have a short slide set (3-4 slides) ready to show cost model assumptions? Rishi — please bring a short list of kernel/quantization caveats for the 13B vs 70B paths.

Thanks — M.

Marissa / team — thanks for the alignment and quick turnaround on scheduling. Confirming the Thu session and that we uploaded: finbot_sample_trace_20260421.json and baseline_perf_sheet.xlsx to the Drive link. We’re especially interested in seeing: a) a split of cost savings by batching vs quantization, and b) guidance on potential accuracy delta for 4-bit on our eval set. We’ll prioritize the high-value flows list by tomorrow morning so you have it for the session.

Thanks again — Alex
